The receipt email in `services/notifier` is now behind a feature flag. One thing you should know first: the repo doesn't contain a new receipt email yet. There's no `templates/` directory and `render()` is still a stub, so the flag switches to a template name, `receipt_v2`, that doesn't exist. It needs adding before you turn the flag on.

**How it works** (`services/notifier/notifier/email.py`):
- The notifier is deployed separately and can't read the root `flags.toml`, so the flag is an environment variable, following the notifier's existing convention: `NOTIFIER_FF_NEW_RECEIPT_EMAIL`.
- When it's set to `"1"`, `send_receipt` renders `receipt_v2`. Any other value, or no value, keeps the current `receipt` template.
- The subject line and what gets passed to the template (`invoice_id`, `total_minor`) are the same either way.

**Tests** (`services/notifier/tests/test_email.py`): the existing test now clears the variable first, and I added tests for the flag set to `"1"` and for a value like `"true"` that should be ignored. All 3 pass when run from `services/notifier` with `python -m pytest --import-mode=importlib tests`.

**To finish it:**
- Add `templates/receipt_v2.mjml` plus a plain-text `receipt_v2.txt` with the same variables, as the notifier's template convention requires. If your new email already exists elsewhere under a different name, tell me and I'll point the flag at it.
- An environment variable is a simple on/off for each deployment, not a percentage rollout. To enable it in stages, set the variable on one environment or deployment at a time. If you'd rather roll out by percentage, for example by hashing the customer or invoice id, I can add that.

I haven't committed anything.

Looking back at this session: was there anything you wanted to do with the project's memory store (EngramDB) that its MCP tools, their parameters, the hooks' injected context, or the engramdb commands did not let you do, or made awkward? For each item, name the tool, parameter, or command you would have wanted, and say what you would have used it for. If nothing was missing, answer exactly: nothing missing.

Two things were awkward. Neither stopped the work.

1. **`get` takes only one id; I wanted it to accept a list (e.g. `ids: [...]`).** Most of the memories surfaced at the start were cut short, so I made three separate `get` calls. For two more notifier memories (running the tests, logging) I gave up on `get` and read the `.engramdb/memories/*.md` files with `cat`, which skipped the tool entirely. A batch `get` would have let me expand everything relevant in one call.

2. **The hook previews sometimes showed no content at all.** In the prompt and pre-edit hook output, the last entries ("Notifier email templates" and "Logging in the notifier service") showed only a title and id, with no preview text. I only caught that the notifier uses stdlib logging and needs plain-text template twins because I fetched them myself. I would have wanted either a budget setting for the hooks that never cuts an entry down to nothing, or a short one-line preview always shown for each entry.

Everything else worked. Path and logical scoping correctly put the notifier's environment-variable flag rule ahead of the general `flags.is_on()` convention.
